desk_read: Yesterday's session was characterized by widespread short covering alongside above-average volumes across multiple asset classes. In energy markets, WTI Crude Oil and Brent saw modest price gains of +0.34% and +0.03% respectively, accompanied by falling total open interest and backwardated curves, pointing to short covering. Equity indexes like the Nasdaq 100 rallied +1.25% on volume at 1.7x its 20-day average while total open interest fell -726 contracts (-0.2%), also reflecting short covering against a contango curve structure. Meanwhile, Gold faced long liquidation with a price decline of -0.94%, total open interest dropping -4.8k contracts (-1.2%), and volume running at 1.4x its 20-day average.
oil_read: Yesterday, WTI (CLZ26) rose +0.34% with total open interest falling -2.8k contracts (-0.2%) and volume at 1.2x its 20-day average, signaling short covering amid a backwardated curve where the CLZ26-CLK27 spread stood at +7.47 $/bbl (-1.20 vs previous session). Brent (NYMEX, BZF27) gained +0.03% with total open interest down -98 contracts (-0.1%) and volume at 1.4x its 20-day average, also showing short covering and backwardation with a BZF27-BZM27 spread of +10.54 $/bbl (-1.65 vs previous session).
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil holds a neutral bias driven by short covering, while Brent sits at mildly bullish on short covering.
